checks: dk, k, d3 grow monotonically with d1 (non-decreasing; 3/3.2 and 4.8/5 share dk/k by standard)
d3 (hole) = d1 + 0.1 for 3..6 and d1 + 0.1 for 2.4/6.4 (2.5, 6.5): hole always slightly larger than body
dk/d1 ratio 1.9-2.2 (flat dome head about twice shank diameter) for every row
k < dk/4 for every row (low dome)
Cross-checked d3 against Westfield Table 4: identical for all 8 sizes
shape_hint: Open-end blind (pop) rivet: a plain cylindrical tubular body of diameter d1 with a low dome (pan) head of diameter dk and small height k at one end; a thin steel mandrel (break stem) passes through the bore and protrudes from the head side, snapping off after setting. The body is drawn straight (pre-set) and the length L is chosen from the grip range.
notes: Values are DIN 7337 (Form A, dome head) nominals as printed by 3 independent pages. Wuerth and theo-schrauben, which label the same part DIN EN ISO 15977, print identical dk/k/d3 for 3-6.4 but theo lists k=0.7 for 2.4 (row 2.4 keeps k=0.55 as agreed by Westfield, boltsfastener, yiwan; 0.7 = 0.55+0.15 tolerance = k max). Other vendors (Keller-Kalmbach ISO 15977 product pages) list k as roughly nominal+tolerance (k_max: 3.2:1.0, 4:1.3, 4.8:1.4), and dk 6.3 for d=3/3.2 - so ISO 15977 max-limit values are NOT the same numbers; do not mix. Sizes 3 and 5 and 6 are metric-only sizes (3.0/5.0/6.0); 2.4/3.2/4.8/6.4 correspond to inch 3/32,1/8,3/16,1/4. Row 3.2: boltsfastener has hole typo '63.3' so only 3 sources support the full row (Westfield, yiwan, theo).

verification.checks_done: Re-fetched Westfield, boltsfastener, yiwan, theo and Wuerth PDF (read with PyMuPDF) live. Westfield Table 1 decoded from the real colspan/rowspan attributes (d1 metric row 3,4,5,6 + imperial row 2.4,3.2,4.8,6.4; d2 5,6.5(x2),8,9.5(x2),12,13; k 0.55,0.8(x2),1,1.1(x2),1.5,1.8) - decode is exact; Table 4 d3 gives all 8 values explicitly. 8 rows x 3 data cols = 24 cells. Clusters per cell (non-PDF): dk 4 for 2.4-4.8, 3 for 5/6/6.4; k 4 for 3,3.2,4,4.8, 3 for 2.4 (theo 0.7 dissents) and 5/6/6.4; d3 4 for 2.4,3,4,4.8, 3 for 3.2 (Westfield, yiwan, theo; boltsfastener typo '63.3') and 5/6/6.4. Wuerth PDF equals the record for 4.8,5,6,6.4 (dk 9.5,9.5,12,13; k 1.1,1.1,1.5,1.8; hole 4.9,5.1,6.1,6.5) but is not counted. No dissent besides theo k(2.4)=0.7 and the boltsfastener typo. Physical: monotone, d3=d1+0.1, dk/d1 1.9-2.2.
problems: Rows 5, 6, 6.4 (all three columns) and k of 2.4 rest on exactly Westfield + boltsfastener + yiwan. yiwan is a marketing blog whose numbers equal Westfield's with no distinguishing typo, so its independence is unproven (not provable either way).

boltsfastener page heading says 'Countersunk head Open Type Blind Rivets' although the numbers (k 0.55 ... d2 5 ...) are the dome-head DIN 7337 values; heading judged a mislabel (a countersunk head with d2=5, d1=2.4 would have k>0.7). 'Drill dia.' is the d3 hole; its 3.2 value is the typo '63.3'.

d3 of row 3.2 needs the German dataset (Wuerth-derived product list) as 3rd cluster. That table is vendor product data under the ISO 15977 label; its Kopfhoehe for 2.4 (0.7) is k max, for 3-4.8 it equals k nominal - i.e. its k semantics are inconsistent, so it is not trusted for k. If the lead refuses theo/Wuerth-derived data, drop row 3.2 (d3 would have only Westfield + yiwan) - not done here because the German dataset is an HTML source under the lead's own rule.
Supplementary (not counted): rivetfast.com hole table equals all 8 d3 values but its head diameters are generic and wrong; fasteners.eu DIN 7337 has d2 only for 3.0,3.2,4.0,4.8,5.0 (agrees).
Producer status 'ok' is right only because of the 3-source minimum above; producer row_support (4) wrongly counts the Wuerth PDF for rows 5,6,6.4.
